Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to start the run chase as the players and the Umpires make their way to the middle. Namibia Under-19 come out to chase 134 runs to win the game and it is Johannes De Villiers and Gerhard Van Rensburg to open the batting for them. Garuka Sanketh to start the attack for Sri Lanka Under-19. Let's Play!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Namibia Under-19's dominance extended beyond their bowling prowess, as their fielding unit complemented the bowlers' efforts admirably. The players showcased sharp fielding skills, consistently grabbing crucial catches and providing solid support to the bowlers. Zacheo Vuuren emerged as the chief tormentor, bagging 4 wickets, while Johannes De Villiers contributed significantly with 3 crucial dismissals. Now, with the target set at 134 runs, the focus shifts to Namibia's batting lineup, poised to chase down the total and secure a vital victory in this ICC U19 World Cup encounter. The question that lingers: Will the Namibian batters rise to the occasion and successfully accomplish the task at hand? Only time will unveil the answer to this intriguing cricketing saga. Stay tuned as the run chase in coming up soon.

Peter-Daniel Blignaut is in for a chat. He starts by saying this is his first wicket of the tournament and he is delighted to have one under the belt. Explains that the pitch is turning a lot. He focused on bowling a lot slower and hit his lengths. Mentions they know the deck is a bit up and down. Feels that his team will be able to chase it down, hopes that they remain smart and keep rotating the strike.

Sri Lanka Under-19 innings unfolded at a sluggish pace, with the openers managing only 4 runs in the initial 6 overs. Although they navigated through the powerplay, the Namibian bowlers struck swiftly, dismissing the openers and setting the tone for a challenging innings. The lone shining light for Sri Lanka was Supun Waduge, who entered the fray at number 3 and displayed commendable resilience, scoring an unbeaten 56 off 79 balls. His valiant effort, which included 6 boundaries, out of the 9 in total boundaries of the innings, stood out amidst a batting lineup that struggled to make a significant impact. With extras contributing 25 runs, no other Sri Lankan batter managed to break free, resulting in their eventual downfall as they were bowled out for 133 runs.

That brings us to the end of the first innings where Namibia Under-19, after winning the toss and choosing to bowl first bowled out Sri Lanka Under-19 at just 133 runs in 37.5 overs in the match number 12 of the ICC Under 19 World Cup 2024. The wicket was helpful for the bowlers and Namibia bowled well and kept picking up wickets at regular intervals, not letting Sri Lanka build any partnership. Now Namibia has the task of chasing down 134 in their quota of 50 overs.

OUT! CAUGHT! Jack Brassell wins this battle and picks up his first wicket of the day. Sri Lanka Under-19 have been bundled out for 133 runs here. A top-class performance from Namibia Under-19. They dominated from the get go. Talking about the wicket. It was a short ball, angled into the bodyline. Garuka Sanketh stays inside the line and tries to help it towards the fine leg region. Although, he only manages to nick it to the right of the wicket-keeper. Johannes Visagie behind the stumps takes a brilliant catch by timing his run to his right.

Commentary.Commentary: Drinks break. Uff! What a contest this has been. Namibian bowlers are all over the opposition here. Sri Lanka Under-19 certainly in a spot of bother as they are teetering at 98/6. This 6th wicket partnership was just starting to grow for them but Namibia Under-19 has always found a way through in this contest to have the upper hand, and once again an inspiring bowling change from the skipper does the trick for them. Sri Lanka Under-19 needs to bat till the very end if they wish to put a competitive total on the board. Let's see what Malsha Tharupathi can do, as he comes in at number 8.

OUT! LBW! Change in bowling working for Namibia Under-19 as Johannes De Villiers picks up a wicket and breaks the partnership on the first ball itself. Tosses the ball up on the off stump line and gets it to nab into the middle stump with pace. Sharujan Shanmuganathan gets stuck on the crease and looks to turn the bat and play the ball on the leg side for a single, in the end misses out on any contact with the bat and the ball rushes onto his his front pads right infront of the wickets. Commentary.Commentary: The national anthems are done and dusted and we are all set for the game to commence. The sun is shining in its full glory as the two umpires make their way out to the centre. Namibia Under-19 are seen in a pre-game huddle near the ropes before they stride out to the centre. It will be the Sri Lankan skipper, Sineth Jayawardena to open the innings alongside Pulindu Perera. Junior Kariata is at the top of his mark and he is raring to go. Here we go...

We are nearing the start of this encounter but before that, Sineth Jayawardena and Alexander Volschenk will lead their respective sides out along with their mascots for the national anthems. It will be Namibia's national anthem first followed by the national anthem of Sri Lanka.

PITCH REPORT - Tino Mawoyo is near the deck. He says that it is a pleasant morning and informs that pitch number 5 will be used for this game. Scott Styris joins him and says that it is a bit different-looking surface than what we had in match number 2 but feels that the characteristics will be the same. Adds that there is a good covering of grass on a good length but as we go down, there are bare patches. Feels that the pitch will be on the slower side and it will also seam a bit early on. Reckons that it is a two-paced surface and batting will not be easy, which aids the decision of Namibia Under-19 to bowl first.

The skipper of Sri Lanka Under-19, Sineth Jayawardena says that they were looking to bowl first as well as the wicket is a bit tacky and will help the fast bowlers in the first 10 overs or so. He adds on by saying that the wicket gets better as the game goes on and it gets easier to chase on this wicket. Ends by saying that they have one change as they replaced a top-order batter with another top-order batter.

The captain of Namibia Under-19, Alexander Volschenk says that they will bowl first. Reckons that there will be something in it for the bowlers early on. Adds that the pitch looks spicy and a bit tacky. Feels that Australia bowled really well in the last game and his batters will learn how to play pace and bounce. Informs that they are going with the same team as the last game with 5 batters, 2 all-rounders and 4 bowlers.
